method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the ACSQHC Delirium Clinical Care Standard, including the eight quality statements and the for-clinicians sections. No antipsychotic agent or dose is asserted; the standard defers to Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic. The multicomponent prevention intervention list was truncated in retrieval and is recorded as input_unavailable rather than reconstructed. Some retrieved text contains extraction artefacts where double-n collapsed ('pla ed' for planned, 'ca ot' for cannot, 'examinatio' for examination); source_text is preserved verbatim and the guideline renders the evident word.

claims.claim: Quality statement 7 states that antipsychotic medicines are not recommended to treat delirium and that behavioural and psychological symptoms in a patient with delirium are managed using non-drug strategies
claims.source_text: Antipsychotic medicines are not recommended to treat delirium. Behavioural and psychological symptoms in a patient with delirium are managed using non-drug strategies.

claims.claim: Evidence does not support the routine use of antipsychotics for treating delirium
claims.source_text: Evidence does not support the routine use of antipsychotics for treating delirium.

claims.claim: Short-term antipsychotic use may be considered in limited circumstances, for instance when non-drug strategies are unsuccessful and there is an imminent risk of the patient harming themselves or others
claims.source_text: However short-term antipsychotic use may be considered in limited circumstances - for instance, when non-drug strategies are unsuccessful and there is an imminent risk of the patient harming themselves or others.

claims.claim: In such cases clinicians should assess the potential harms and benefits of prescribing an antipsychotic and whenever possible discuss the use of the medicine with the patient and family and obtain informed consent, using the lowest appropriate dose for the shortest possible duration, and a single dose is usually enough
claims.source_text: In such cases, assess the potential harms and benefits of prescribing an antipsychotic and, whenever possible, discuss the use of the medicine with the patient and family and obtain informed consent. Use the lowest appropriate dose for the shortest possible duration, as described in Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic.A single dose is usually enough.

claims.claim: When an antipsychotic medicine has been used in an emergency situation the use should be discussed with the patient and their family or carer so they understand why it was used
claims.source_text: When an antipsychotic medicine has been used in an emergency situation, discuss the use with the patient and their family or carer, so they understand why it was used.

claims.claim: If an antipsychotic is prescribed for more than a single dose the plan for the duration of therapy and the criteria for cessation, that is the change in behaviour to be achieved, should be documented
claims.source_text: If an antipsychotic is prescribed for a longer duration (more than a single dose), document the plan for the duration of therapy and the criteria for cessation - that is, the change in behaviour to be achieved.

claims.claim: The patient and their family or carer should be advised that longer-term use of antipsychotics has a greater risk of harm than of benefit except in limited circumstances
claims.source_text: Advise the patient and their family or carer that longer-term use of antipsychotics has a greater risk of harm than of benefit, except in limited circumstances.

claims.claim: Psychiatry or geriatric review should be arranged for a patient with delirium who has other indications for antipsychotic use or who has an existing prescription for antipsychotics
claims.source_text: Arrange psychiatry or geriatric review for a patient with delirium who has other indications for antipsychotic use, or who has an existing prescription for antipsychotics.

claims.claim: Benzodiazepines should be avoided when managing delirium as complications are common and long-acting benzodiazepines increase delirium
claims.source_text: Avoid benzodiazepines when managing delirium, as complications are common and long-acting benzodiazepines increase delirium.

claims.claim: Physical or mechanical restraints should be avoided as they can increase agitation, prolong delirium and increase the risk of injury
claims.source_text: Avoid using physical or mechanical restraints, as they can increase agitation, prolong delirium and increase the risk of injury.

claims.claim: Over-sedation can have serious consequences such as dehydration, falls, respiratory depression, pneumonia and death
claims.source_text: Over-sedation can have serious consequences, such as dehydration, falls, respiratory depression, pneumonia and death.

claims.claim: People with Parkinson's disease or with Lewy body dementia are at an increased risk of severe adverse reactions from antipsychotics
claims.source_text: People with Parkinson's disease or with Lewy body dementia are at an increased risk of severe adverse reactions from antipsychotics.

claims.claim: Key risk factors for delirium include age 65 years or over, or 45 years or over for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people
claims.source_text: age >=65 years (>=45 years for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people)

claims.claim: Other key risk factors are known cognitive impairment or diagnosed dementia, a previous diagnosis of delirium, a severe medical illness meaning a clinical condition that is deteriorating or at risk of deterioration, and current hip fracture
claims.source_text: known cognitive impairment or diagnosed dementia; a previous diagnosis of delirium; a severe medical illness (a clinical condition that is deteriorating or is at risk of deterioration); current hip fracture.

claims.claim: A delirium risk assessment should be conducted in the pre-admission clinic or within 24 hours of presentation to hospital for admitted patients
claims.source_text: Conduct a delirium risk assessment in the pre-admission clinic or within 24 hours of presentation to hospital for admitted patients.

claims.claim: Patients with any key risk factor should receive a validated screening test for cognitive impairment, which is recognised as a significant risk factor for developing delirium
claims.source_text: Patients with any of these risk factors should receive a validated screening test for cognitive impairment, which is recognised as a significant risk factor for developing delirium.

claims.claim: Conducting cognitive screening on presentation to hospital helps identify patients who should be assessed for delirium and enables monitoring for delirium onset during a hospital stay by providing a baseline measure, and this also applies to patients with known cognitive impairment
claims.source_text: Conducting cognitive screening on presentation to hospital helps identify patients who should be assessed for delirium and enables monitoring for delirium onset during a hospital stay by providing a baseline measure. This also applies to patients with known cognitive impairment.

claims.claim: Screening for cognitive impairment should use a validated tool that is culturally appropriate
claims.source_text: Offer screening for cognitive impairment using a validated tool that is culturally appropriate.

claims.claim: Before any planned admission the risk of delirium is assessed and discussed with the patient to enable an informed decision about the benefits and risks
claims.source_text: Before any pla ed admission, the risk of delirium is assessed and discussed with the patient, to enable an informed decision about the benefits and risks.

claims.claim: Quality statement 2 states that a patient at risk of delirium is offered a set of interventions to prevent delirium and is regularly monitored for changes in behaviour, cognition and physical condition, with appropriate interventions determined before a planned admission or on admission in discussion with the patient and their family or carer
claims.source_text: A patient at risk of delirium is offered a set of interventions to prevent delirium and is regularly monitored for changes in behaviour, cognition and physical condition. Appropriate interventions are determined before a pla ed admission or on admission to hospital, in discussion with the patient and their family or carer.

claims.claim: A delirium prevention plan should be developed in partnership with the patient and family or carer as part of a comprehensive care plan for those at risk
claims.source_text: Develop a delirium prevention plan, in partnership with the patient and family or carer, as part of a comprehensive care plan for those at risk of developing delirium.

claims.claim: Family or carers should be encouraged to be involved, for example to orient and reassure the patient, and should be asked to alert the healthcare team to any changes in the patient's mental or physical condition
claims.source_text: Discuss the interventions being put in place and encourage family or carers to be involved (for example, to orient and reassure the patient). Ask the family or carer to alert the healthcare team to any changes in the patient's mental or physical condition.

claims.claim: Patients and family or carers should be educated about delirium before it occurs to reduce distress if it does occur
claims.source_text: Educate patients and family or carers about delirium before it occurs, to reduce distress if it does occur.

claims.claim: Patients should be monitored regularly, at least daily, for changes in cognition and behaviour and for clinical deterioration
claims.source_text: Monitor patients regularly, at least daily for changes in cognition and behaviour, and for clinical deterioration.

claims.claim: Risk of delirium is increased post-operatively
claims.source_text: Risk of delirium is increased post-operatively.

claims.claim: Medication reconciliation should be conducted before patients are transferred between locations or phases of care such as before moving between wards or transferring to another facility
claims.source_text: Conduct medication reconciliation before patients are transferred between locations, or phases of care (such as before moving between wards or transferring to another facility).

claims.claim: Identifying hypoactive, hyperactive or mixed cases of delirium is necessary to implement appropriate treatment strategies, and hypoactive delirium is more common in older people but is often missed and has a worse prognosis than other subtypes including worse long-term cognition when delirium has a longer duration
claims.source_text: Identifying hypoactive, hyperactive or mixed cases of delirium is necessary to implement appropriate treatment strategies. Hypoactive delirium is more common in older people, but is often missed and has a worse prognosis than other subtypes of delirium, including worse long-term cognition when delirium has a longer duration.

claims.claim: Delirium is less likely to be recognised in patients with frailty or dementia
claims.source_text: Delirium is less likely to be recognised in patients with frailty or dementia.

claims.claim: Quality statement 4 requires that a patient with cognitive impairment on presentation to hospital, or who has an acute change in behaviour or cognitive function during a hospital stay, is promptly assessed using a validated tool by a clinician trained to assess delirium, that the patient and family or carer are asked about recent changes in behaviour or thinking, and that a diagnosis is determined and documented by a clinician working within their scope of practice
claims.source_text: A patient with cognitive impairment on presentation to hospital, or who has an acute change in behaviour or cognitive function during a hospital stay, is promptly assessed using a validated tool by a clinician trained to assess delirium. The patient and their family or carer are asked about any recent changes in the patient's behaviour or thinking. A diagnosis of delirium is determined and documented by a clinician working within their scope of practice.

claims.claim: Information about the patient's usual mental status should be sought from the patient or their family or carer, general practitioner or other primary care provider
claims.source_text: Seek information about the patient's usual mental status from the patient or their family or carer, general practitioner, or other primary care provider or similar.

claims.claim: Behavioural changes to ask about include confusion or worsened concentration, agitation or restlessness, sleepiness including altered levels of consciousness, whether the patient has been less communicative or less responsive than usual, and whether the patient has had difficulty cooperating with reasonable requests or other alterations in mood
claims.source_text: Ask about behavioural changes, such as: confusion or worsened concentratio ; agitation or restlessness; sleepiness, including altered levels of consciousness; whether the patient has been less communicative or less responsive than usual; whether the patient has had difficulty cooperating with reasonable requests or has had other alterations in mood.

claims.claim: Family members or carers are often the best source of information about acute changes in a patient's mental status or behaviour
claims.source_text: Family members or carers are often the best source of information about acute changes in a patient's mental status or behaviour.

claims.claim: As delirium symptoms can vary throughout the day more than one assessment may be required to diagnose delirium
claims.source_text: As delirium symptoms can vary throughout the day, more than one assessment may be required to diagnose delirium.

claims.claim: The diagnosis should be documented to aid in transfers of care including in handover notes, referral and discharge letters, because a history of delirium increases the risk of recurrence and documenting an episode allows for preventive measures and monitoring for new delirium in subsequent healthcare encounters
claims.source_text: Document the diagnosis to aid in transfers of care, including in handover notes, referral and discharge letters. A history of delirium increases the risk of recurrence, and documenting an episode of delirium allows for preventive measures and monitoring for new delirium in subsequent healthcare encounters.

claims.claim: The diagnosis should be discussed with the patient and their family or carer, and current international clinical guidelines include validated delirium diagnostic tools some of which require training to use effectively
claims.source_text: Discuss the diagnosis with the patient and their family or carer. Current international clinical guidelines include validated delirium diagnostic tools, some of which require training to use the tool effectively.

claims.claim: Quality statement 5 states that a patient with delirium is offered a set of interventions to treat the causes of delirium based on a comprehensive assessment that includes relevant multidisciplinary consultation
claims.source_text: A patient with delirium is offered a set of interventions to treat the causes of delirium, based on a comprehensive assessment that includes relevant multidisciplinary consultation.

claims.claim: A patient summary should be sought from the patient's general practitioner to help inform the investigation
claims.source_text: Seek a patient summary from the patient's general practitioner to help inform the investigation.

claims.claim: A comprehensive assessment involves a medical and social history paying close attention to medication history including adverse reactions, pain management needs and hydration and nutritional status; a physical examination; investigations informed by the history and examination; and consultation with other clinicians with relevant expertise such as a geriatrician, psychiatrist or dietitian whenever possible, which in rural and remote health services could be facilitated by telehealth
claims.source_text: a medical and social history, paying close attention to the patient's medication history, including adverse reactions, their pain management needs, and their hydration and nutritional status; a physical examinatio ; investigations, informed by the medical history and physical examinatio ; consultation with other clinicians with relevant expertise (such as a geriatrician, psychiatrist, dietitian), whenever possible. In rural and remote health services this could be facilitated by using telehealth when information technology systems allow.

claims.claim: Prevention is the most effective strategy but outcomes for patients with delirium can also be improved by early intervention
claims.source_text: Prevention is the most effective strategy, but outcomes for patients with delirium can also be improved by early intervention.

claims.claim: Quality statement 6 states that a patient with delirium receives care to prevent functional decline, dehydration, malnutrition, falls and pressure injuries based on their risk, and that these risks should be assessed, monitored and documented
claims.source_text: A patient with delirium receives care to prevent functional decline, dehydration, malnutrition, falls and pressure injuries, based on their risk. ... If a patient has delirium, assess, monitor and document their risks of: functional decline; falling and being harmed from a fall; developing a pressure injury, dehydration or malnutrition.

claims.claim: Examples of interventions for falls prevention include reorientation, appropriate lighting and ensuring that patients are using their eyeglasses or hearing aids
claims.source_text: Examples of interventions for falls prevention can include reorientation, appropriate lighting and ensuring that patients are using their eyeglasses or hearing aids.

claims.claim: To lessen the risk of functional decline mobility and self-care should be encouraged with assistance as necessary
claims.source_text: To lessen the risk of functional decline, encourage mobility and self-care with assistance as necessary.

claims.claim: Patients should be assisted as required throughout the day to maintain optimal nutrition and hydration, dentures should be fitted correctly particularly at mealtimes, and a dietitian should assess and manage patients at risk of malnutrition
claims.source_text: Assist patients as required throughout the day to ensure that they maintain optimal nutrition and hydration. Ensure dentures are fitted correctly, particularly at mealtimes. For patients at risk of malnutrition, arrange for a dietitian to assess and manage them.

claims.claim: Quality statement 3 states that a patient at risk of delirium and their family or carer are encouraged to be active participants in care, that those at significant risk or with delirium are provided with information about delirium and its prevention in a way they can understand, and that when delirium occurs they receive support to cope with the experience and its effects
claims.source_text: A patient at risk of delirium and their family or carer are encouraged to be active participants in care. If a patient is at significant risk or has, delirium, they and their family or carer are provided with information about delirium and its prevention in a way that they can understand. When delirium occurs, they receive support to cope with the experience and its effects.

claims.claim: Clinicians should recognise when to engage an interpreting service, and family or friends may not be appropriate interpreters because of health privacy issues
claims.source_text: Recognise when to engage an interpreting service to ensure the patient, families and carers understand the information you are sharing with them. Family or friends may not be appropriate interpreters because of health privacy issues.

claims.claim: If a patient develops delirium clinicians should proactively assess their distress and inform them and their family or carer about the plans to treat and reduce the severity of symptoms and any distress experienced
claims.source_text: If a patient develops delirium, proactively assess their distress and inform them and their family or carer about the plans to treat and reduce the severity of symptoms and any distress experienced with delirium.

claims.claim: Patients should be supported to make their own decisions and to choose a support person to be involved in decisions
claims.source_text: Support patients to make their own decisions and to choose a support person to be involved in decisions.

claims.claim: Clinicians should ask patients specifically about fears or concerns and about hallucinations, and reassure patients and help them feel safe
claims.source_text: Ask patients specifically about fears or concerns, and about hallucinations. Reassure patients and help them feel safe.

claims.claim: For a patient with severe behavioural or emotional disturbance clinicians should investigate possible causes by conducting a comprehensive assessment including a medication review, identify medicines known to contribute to delirium such as those with anticholinergic or sedative properties and adjust if appropriate, and ensure that any medical causes for distress and agitation such as pain, constipation, urinary retention and hypoxia are treated
claims.source_text: Investigate possible causes by conducting a comprehensive assessment that includes a medication review. Identify medicines that are known to contribute to delirium and adjust if appropriate, such as medicines with anticholinergic or sedative properties. Ensure that any medical causes for distress and agitation, such as pain, constipation, urinary retention and hypoxia, are treated.

claims.claim: Clinicians should reassure the patient and offer non-drug strategies involving family or carers if possible, or one-on-one nursing, to calm the patient and de-escalate the situation
claims.source_text: Reassure the patient and offer non-drug strategies - involving family or carers, if possible, or one-on-one nursing - to calm the patient and de-escalate the situation.

claims.claim: Information about the patient, their needs and preferences and ways to reduce distress should be obtained, and if the patient cannot provide it themselves clinicians should engage family or carers and use a structured tool such as the TOP 5 model
claims.source_text: Obtain information about the patient, their needs and preferences, and ways to reduce distress. If the patient ca ot provide the information themselves, engage with family or carers, and use a structured tool such as the TOP 5 model.

claims.claim: The environment should be safe for the patient, noise minimised, and the patient observed without staff invading their personal space
claims.source_text: Ensure that the environment is safe for the patient and that noise is minimised, and the patient is observed without the staff invading their personal space.

claims.claim: Verbal and non-verbal de-escalation techniques include being respectful, introducing yourself and using their title rather than their given name if the patient does not know you, talking slowly and calmly, not disagreeing with the patient, asking questions and listening to the answers, expressing empathy and concern, inclining your head slightly to show you are listening and to give a non-threatening posture, acknowledging their feelings and that the situation is frightening or distressing, and providing a distraction
claims.source_text: being respectful; introducing yourself and using their title rather than their given name if the patient does not know you; talking slowly and calmly; not disagreeing with the patient; asking questions and listening to the answers; expressing empathy and concern to show that you have understood; inclining your head slightly, to show you are listening and to give you a non-threatening posture; acknowledging their feelings and that the situation they find themselves in is frightening or distressing; providing a distraction.

claims.claim: Quality statement 8 requires that before a patient with persistent or resolved delirium leaves hospital an individualised comprehensive care plan is developed collaboratively with the patient and their family or carer describing post-discharge care needs and including strategies to reduce the risk of delirium and related complications, a summary of changes in medicines and any other ongoing treatment
claims.source_text: Before a patient with persistent or resolved delirium leaves hospital, an individualised comprehensive care plan is developed collaboratively with the patient and their family or carer. The plan describes the patient's post-discharge care needs and includes strategies to help reduce the risk of delirium and related complications, a summary of changes in medicines and any other ongoing treatment.

claims.claim: The care plan is provided to the patient and their family or carer before discharge and to their general practitioner and other regular clinicians within 48 hours of discharge
claims.source_text: This plan is provided to the patient and their family or carer before discharge, and to their general practitioner and other regular clinicians within 48 hours of discharge.

claims.claim: The plan should include a plan for review by a specialist clinic, specialist or primary healthcare provider 10 days after discharge
claims.source_text: Include a plan for review by a specialist clinic, specialist or primary healthcare provider 10 days after discharge.

claims.claim: All medicines the patient needs to take should be listed specifying the generic drug name, dose, reason for use and duration for each one, and clinicians should explain why any medicines have been stopped or changed
claims.source_text: List all medicines that the patient needs to take, specifying the generic drug name, dose, reason for use and duration for each one. Explain why any medicines have been stopped or changed.

claims.claim: All ongoing treatments and any follow-up needed for comorbidities should be described, appropriate outpatient rehabilitation services arranged when required, and the patient advised of ongoing support services in the community with contact details as appropriate
claims.source_text: Describe all ongoing treatments and any follow-up needed for any comorbidities. Arrange appropriate outpatient rehabilitation services when required. ... Advise the patient of ongoing support services in the community and provide contact details, as appropriate.

claims.claim: The multicomponent interventions recommended for preventing delirium should also be in place to manage delirium, including involving family or carers and modifying the environment
claims.source_text: Ensure that the multicomponent interventions recommended for preventing delirium are also in place to manage delirium, including involving family or carers and modifying the environment
